data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'shyama' meaning dark and 'taka' meaning lord, Shyamantak symbolizes the god of darkness. The name Shyamantak carries the meaning “God of Darkness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shyamantak usually hope their child will grow to embody god of darkness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna and Shiva are known to have various names and forms, representing differing aspects of the divine. Shyamantak, as a name, resonates deep in the rich cultural fabric of India, a testament to the acceptance of diverse and sometimes contradictory aspects of the divine. The root of the name, 'shyama' meaning dark, is also associated with Lord Shiva, who is typically depicted as adorned in ash, symbolizing the enormity of the universe and the infinite darkness of space.
data.spiritual_significance: Shyamantak, as a name, embodies the idea of the all-pervading darkness that underlies the fabric of the universe. It serves as a reminder of the existential realities of life, the depth and mystery of the universe, and the obscure nature of the divine. The spiritual significance of the name is rooted in the Sanskrit word 'tapa' which means 'penance' or 'austerity', indicating the worship and reverence of the divine manifested as the darkest force. Through this name, Shyamantak, we are invited to explore and honor the divine within the enigma of darkness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shyamantak: God of inexhaustible wealth and prosperity. His name symbolizes the endless abundance and blessings bestowed upon his devotees. The one who chants "Shyamantak" is believed to be constantly filled with the riches of love, knowledge, and spiritual growth.
